rulebook.name: Turtle S2 inspired equity daily adaptation
rulebook.sourceEra: 1983–1988 original futures program; publicly documented original rules 2003; research daily equity adaptation

provenance.description: 55 prior-session highest high; source takes intraday price break, this engine evaluates closing price strictly above prior high.
20 prior-session lowest low exit-channel concept.
N20 seeds with 20 true ranges then updates (19*N+TR)/20.
One source unit risks 1% equity for a 1N move: share unit = 0.01*equity/N.
Initial stop concept is actual execution fill minus 2 pre-signal N, not a future-day low.
Closed daily signals execute at next session open; stop only closes below known level, no intraday orders.
Use prior-day N daily and signal-close reference price for planned weight; cap each ticker at 10%, maximum ten, cash-only. Actual fill may change realized initial risk.
Long-only equities; one unit with no pyramid, no correlated-market limits, no annual notional-account drawdown haircut; deterministic security-id ordering.

rulebook.name: Weinstein inspired daily stage adaptation
rulebook.sourceEra: 1988 stage-analysis investor concepts; public secondary book excerpts; research daily equity adaptation

provenance.description: Stage 2 means price above a rising 30-week average; avoid buying below a falling average.
Resistance break supported by volume and relative strength; market direction matters.
Source chart-dependent support stops are not a fixed universal percent or basis low.
150-session daily SMA substitutes 30 weeks; rising means current SMA above SMA20 sessions earlier, for stock and supplied market.
Close strictly above prior50-session high; prior-base width <=30%; signal-day volume >=1.5*prior20 average.
Stock63-session close-price return exceeds same-date market return; this is not source Mansfield RS.
Initial stop level 1% below prior50-session lowest low; close below known stop or daily SMA150 triggers next-open exit; no trailing swing logic.
Fixed10% each, maximum ten, cash-only, no short side, half-position pullback or industry selection; deterministic security-id ordering.
